title: Model Onboarding Decision Flow for Encumbered / Restricted Weights
creator: Priya Nambiar
description:
Problem: Customers and internal teams are onboarding models whose published weights are encumbered (restricted licenses, embargoes, or dual-licensed artifacts). We need a clear, auditable decision flow that combines automated checks and manual legal/safety review so the model catalog and public API only expose models consistent with Redwood policy and enterprise agreements.

Scope: Establish the decision flow, required metadata, automated gating rules, UI indicators in the model catalog, and operational SLAs for manual reviews. This ticket captures the PM-level acceptance criteria, proposed flow, rollout plan, and outstanding questions for Legal/Research/Engineering. It is intentionally focused on policy and product integration (not on kernel/runtime optimizations).

Goals:
- Reduce ambiguity for engineers and customers when a model's weights are legally encumbered.
- Automate low-risk checks to avoid manual review churn.
- Ensure that performance profile publishing and version pinning do not occur until compliance gating is complete.
- Provide clear UI/metadata signals (restricted, enterprise-only, pending-legal) and API flags for clients to handle gracefully.
proposal_summary: 1) Add a metadata classifier run during model upload that extracts license text, model provenance URL(s), and declared restrictions. 2) Compute a risk score: license compatibility + known restricted weight registry matches + provenance completeness. 3) Based on thresholds: auto-approve (public), auto-flag (tenant/enterprise only with warning), or route to Manual Legal Review. 4) Block performance profile publishing and public version pinning until final clearance. 5) Display catalog badges (e.g., RESTRICTED, PENDING_LEGAL, ENTERPRISE_ONLY). 6) Log audit trail to customer workspace and central compliance index. 7) Provide API/CLI response codes and telemetry for downstream enforcement and observability.
acceptance_criteria: A classifier runs on every model upload and stores license metadata + provenance URL in the model record
An automated risk score is computed and visible in the catalog UI and via API
Three gating outcomes implemented: auto-approve, restrict-to-enterprise, or manual-legal-review
Performance profiles are prevented from being published publicly until clearance flag is set
Catalog UI shows a clear badge and explanatory tooltip for any non-auto-approved model
Legal reviews are assigned within 3 business days and decisions are recorded on the model record
Telemetry emits a compliance decision event for downstream metrics and billing teams
rollout_plan: Week 1: Ship metadata extractor + risk scoring prototype behind feature flag for internal uploads
Week 2: Integrate gating outcomes with model catalog UI (badges) and API flags; feature-flag enforcement for hosted catalog
Week 3: Connect manual review work queue to Legal Slack/channel and build audit log persistence
Week 4: Turn on enforcement for non-production customers and monitor false positives/negatives
Week 5: Enterprise beta (dedicated accounts) with adjustable policy thresholds and single-tenant override controls
open_questions: What exact license classifications should map to auto-approve vs manual review? (Legal input required)
Do we accept models where weights are available under noncommercial terms for enterprise customers with signed agreements?
Should performance profiles be generated in a private sandbox automatically (not published) while waiting on legal review?
What SLA will Legal commit to for initial and escalated reviews beyond 3 business days?
How do we surface embargoed-reuse windows (e.g., weights embargoed for X months) in the catalog and API?
notes_and_tradeoffs: Automating the majority of gating reduces review load but increases risk of edge-case approvals. Conservative thresholds will increase manual review volume (slower time to publish) — we should instrument initial false-positive rates for 2 weeks and iterate. We also need to balance developer experience: showing too many blocking messages at upload will discourage self-serve flows. Proposed compromise: soft-warning UX for low-risk flags with clear path to request expedited legal review for customers paying for enterprise SLA.
implementation_guidance: Engineering: add a pipeline stage in the upload service that calls the license classifier (OSS tool) and computes risk score. Store 3 atomic fields on model metadata: license_identifier, weight_registry_match (bool), risk_score (0-100). API: add channel 'compliance_status' with values 'public', 'enterprise_only', 'pending_legal', 'blocked'. Console: show badges + link to the provenance artifact. Ops: add alerts if manual review queue length > 10 or average review time > 3 business days.
dependencies_detail: Depends on PM-6310 (model-source-validation) for provenance ingestion and PM-5234 (playbook/version-gates) for pinning logic. Also requires Legal onboarding and a small Legal UI to approve/deny models; scope for a minimal review UI is included in this ticket.
communication_plan: Announce pilot to internal alpha testers and Enterprise customers via product changelog and partner Slack. Provide a short how-to doc for requesting expedited legal review and an FAQ for common license outcomes.
